phase: Phase 5: The rest of the inventory (after the look check) - step: lily pad (PM order 2026-11-17)
summary: PASS at HEAD 1adac676, at the bar. The lily pad is rated 7.0 out of 10 (bar 7.0). The ten criteria give a mean of 3.5 of 5, so no margin exists. The 3D model and the 128 px sprites read as a lily pad: a round green dish with a V notch. The two delivered cutouts do not. Both are the same edge-on slab (410 x 34 px), because ./forge cutout uses elevation 0 for every view. A 2D scene needs a look-down cutout (N1). The frog fits, with 26 mm of leaf at the haunches, but it fills 87 percent of the pad width (N2). The veins are faint: 7 percent luminance difference (N3). The mechanical checks pass, the scope is clean, and all 5 claims of the plan bullet are true. The brief states the frog depth wrongly (N4).
nonblocking_findings: N1 [Medium] the delivered cutouts cannot show the pad (the maker's first weak point, and wider than the maker says): out/chibi-sprouts/r1/props/lily-pad/front.png and three-quarter.png have the same box, cols 307..716 and rows 974..1007 (410 x 34 px, 13096 and 13146 opaque pixels). The maker log names only the front cutout. The three-quarter cutout is also an edge-on slab, because ./forge cutout sets elevation 0 for every named view unless --el is given (src/cli/forge.ts:383), so the 35 degree azimuth adds nothing. The slab shows no veins and no dish. The notch shows as a recessed block in the middle of the front cutout and as a lighter block at the left end of the three-quarter cutout. At the 128 px scale (1/8) the pad is about 51 x 4 px, a green line. The PM brief calls an edge-on flat prop expected, so this is not a build defect. Whether the files serve week 6 depends on the route. A 3D stage (src/song, a GLB prop) needs no cutout and works as built. The Workbooks 2D compositor needs a look-down view. Suggested change: order one look-down cutout (about --el 35) in a separate folder. One folder keeps one ppm, one canvas, and one foot point (src/cli/forge.ts:393-394 and 416). The near rim falls about 0.2 x sin 35 = 0.115 m, or 117 px at 1024 ppm, below the foot row, so the margin must be about 135 px or more. I did not run this. | owner: orchestrator (route decision), then maker

N2 [Medium] frog fit and scene needs (the PM question): the frog fits, with no spare room. Measured on out/frog/frog.glb (rest pose, feet = vertices with y below 0.03 m): the feet footprint is 0.347 x 0.166 m, and its smallest enclosing circle has radius 0.1736 m about (0.0001, -0.0028). The pad radius is 0.200 m, so the leaf margin is 26 mm at the haunch feet, as the maker says. No foot vertex lies beyond the pad edge. The frog is 0.346 m tall and 0.347 m wide, which is 87 percent of the pad width. With the frog centred, 5 foot vertices (the inner edges of the front feet, x -0.0014 to 0.0087, z 0.0103 to 0.0456) overhang the V by up to 9 mm. A shift of the frog 0.03 m back leaves 1 vertex and a 20 mm margin. The rim has risen only 0.6 mm at r 0.1737 (it starts at r 0.17), so the outer feet stand on nearly flat leaf. From a low camera the frog hides the pad. The scene needs: (a) the pad scaled 1.3 to 1.5 in the stage (a prop scale; margin 86 to 126 mm) or the frog at about 0.7; (b) the frog on the pad top at y about 0.018 (dish 0.016 at the centre, 0.020 at r 0.17), about 0.03 m back of the centre; (c) a camera elevation of 30 degrees or more for the shot, because the stage example key (docs/storytime-song.md:20) uses el 12, which shows the 0.4 m pad as an ellipse only 0.083 m high; (d) the pad green and the pond pad green aligned if both show (assets/pond.ts:18-19 use #7cc23c and #5a9a2a, and this pad uses #5fa364 and #4f8f5a). Out/frog/stats.json lists the clips idle, walk, attack, hit, and death. No hop clip exists, so the hop of line 9 is stage work. | owner: orchestrator (scene)

N3 [Low] faint veins (the maker's second weak point): confirmed. The vein and rim green #4f8f5a has luminance 125.6 against 144.0 for the leaf #5fa364: a difference of 18.4 of 255 (7.2 percent, ratio 0.872). Each vein is 0.006 m wide, about 1.2 px in a 128 px sprite. In the 1x sprite row the veins show as thin lines, and they do not carry the read. The notch and the round dish carry it. In the cutouts the veins are invisible (N1). The maker followed the PM colours. Suggested change, optional: a darker vein (about #3f7f4c) or a width of 0.010 m, if the owner wants veins at 128 px. | owner: orchestrator (PM default)

N4 [Low] imprecise frog text (assets/lily-pad.ts:23-25; briefs/lily-pad.md:55 and 63-64): the Sources row says the frog measures 0.347 m x 0.222 m at the feet, and Known differences says the feet touch the rim at the notch. Measured: 0.347 m is the foot width, but 0.222 m is the depth of the whole body with the head (skin z -0.0929 to 0.1287). The feet footprint is 0.347 x 0.166 m (z -0.0696 to 0.0969). The front toes that come near the V stand at about z 0.087, about 0.09 m from the centre and near the V apex, not at the rim. The 26 mm margin and the 2 cm statement hold. Suggested change: correct the two details in the brief. | owner: maker (measure-jr-green)

N5 [Nit] notch, rim curl, and vein fan (the maker's third and fourth weak points): confirmed, and within the brief. The V edges are plain cuts that step by about one 4.5 mm cell, and the cut face reads as a blocky lighter step in the three-quarter cutout. A real notch is a sharp slit, so this is acceptable. The curl adds 12 mm to a 20 mm slab (32 mm of 400 mm, 8 percent), so the rim reads as a thick rolled edge or a tray, as the PM asked ('so the pad reads in the front view'). The nine veins sit at 30 + 36 x i degrees, a ten-fold fan with the tenth (354 degrees) removed by the notch. The notch is then 6 degrees off the centre of the 72 degree gap: 15 degrees to the next vein on one side and 27 degrees on the other. This is not visible at the scene scale. No change needed now.

Reads as a lily pad at 128 px: YES for the sprites. At 1x on pond blue, all 8 directions read as a green dish with a V notch and faint radial veins; the sprite is 80 to 82 px wide and 45 to 46 px high (sprites/metrics.json). NO for the cutouts: both are an edge-on slab (N1). The 3D renders read well. The top is a pale mint dish under the studio light, the wall is dark green, and the V is crisp. The shape can also read as a pie with a slice cut out, but the green, the veins, and the dish keep it a leaf.

Brief match (assets/lily-pad.ts): width 0.400 m; top at 0.0319 m (0.02 thickness plus a 0.012 curl); dish 0.004 m (topY(0) 0.016 against 0.020 at r 0.17); notch 2 half-spaces at 15 degrees about +Z (z max 0.1926 = 0.2 x cos 15); colours #5fa364 and #4f8f5a; 9 vein strokes of 0.006 m; roughness 0.45; metalness 0; one body, 3812 triangles under 8000; no flower, frog, or water. The veins start 15 mm from the centre (VEIN_IN) and not at the centre. This is a small deviation from 'from the centre'. The code uses thin boxes for the strokes, and the paint recipe is the same (a stencil that crosses the top surface).

Rating lily-pad 7.0 (pass; at the bar): brief match 4, silhouette 3.5, proportion and appeal 3.5, shape language 3.5, value and colour 3, materials 3.5, detail hierarchy 3, technical quality 4, game readiness 3, readability at 128 px 4. The sum is 35.0, the mean is 3.5 of 5, and that gives 7.0 of 10. The result is at the bar with no margin: a drop of 0.5 in any one criterion gives a mean of 6.9. As an estimate, the 3D model and the sprites alone would rate about 7.5, and the cutouts alone about 4.5, because they do not show the pad.

The maker disclosed all four in the log, and also that no frog-on-pad render exists. That disclosure is honest. I made no frog-on-pad render either, and I measured the fit instead (N2).
